evidence: Three concrete retrieval-oriented modes: 'Transcript pile invisible to setup scan' (high/high) — 'the main corpus is transcript/source files, but scan exposes only one summary note, so initialization as-is would underrepresent history.'

'Raw speech is weak decision evidence' (medium/high) — 'Timestamps, missing speakers, VTT blocks, and truncation make retrieval noisy for decisions/actions.' Matches manifest/log evidence and is exactly the transcript-vs-finished-notes distinction the case is built to test.
'Duplicate format collision' (medium/medium) — '06-20 appears as TXT, copy TXT, and VTT, so retrieval can surface redundant or conflicting snippets.' Verified in workspace.
Each mode has a falsifier and a non-moralizing 'Do not infer' guard.
failures: No '## Non-Failures' / '## Ambiguities' sections; the one clean indexable note is never named as a non-failure.
Identical templated 'Retrieval impact' line on all three modes ('weak or misleading retrieval handles for setup and later meeting context'), reused verbatim across other cases.
VTT/TXT timestamp-format mismatch (frame-style vs conversational) is collapsed into 'Duplicate format collision' rather than named as its own temporal-retrieval issue.
patch_recommendation: Mandate Non-Failures/Ambiguities sections and per-mode (non-templated) retrieval impact; this case strongly supports the transcript-vs-notes distinction, which is its best feature and should be preserved.
risk_notes: Best-fit failure model of the three cases (transcript dump is what the modes describe). Gate passes; templated retrieval-impact and missing Non-Failures recur.
